fixture: First-integrator thermal-noise bench (issue #126): design/integrator's full cell held in one clock phase per variant, small-signal .noise over 1 Hz - 1e+11 Hz. ktc = the four sampling capacitors in phi1; amp = the OTA with its phi2 switches, at the differential output; ampq = the same integrate phase read across Ci, i.e. the part that accumulates (issue #140), plus a one-corner per-device split.
result_kind: simulated (ngspice .noise, transistor-level netlists of design/integrator/integrator.spice and design/ota/ota_fd.spice; not the behavioural model). A simulated number is never called measured.
model_b_parameter: ktc_noise_var (sim/bmodel/model.py): per-sampling-event variance in FS^2, added to integrator 1's state increment

method.chosen: `.noise` on the real cell, one of the three forms issue #126 allows and the one DR-001 item 2 names. Not kT/C arithmetic: the simulated variance carries each corner's own capacitance, its switch noise at the bias that phase gives it, and the plate and switch parasitics that arithmetic from the drawn value alone would miss (cs_eff_F below runs +11.0% (fs/1.800V/125C) to +28.8% (fs/1.620V/-40C) against the drawn Cs of 9.9763e-13 F, a 45-corner spread rather than one figure, for exactly that reason).
method.why_three_requests: a small-signal .noise run needs a static clock state and one corner runs one analysis with one output, so the two halves of spec 5.3's thermal share are two requests over the same 45-point grid (as sim/integrator-settling does with int1/int2), and issue #140's accumulating read of the integrate phase is a third over that same grid
method.accumulating_vs_static: issue #140. `amp` reads v(vod) in the static phi2 state and refers it to the integrator input by 1/C1. That is right for noise that is sampled independently each cycle, but v(vod) also carries the summing-node excursion, which the next phi1 reset discards: what accumulates is the charge left on Ci. `ampq` is the SAME state and the SAME 1/C1 referral read across Ci instead, so it measures the per-cycle output increment directly, and the per-corner ratio of the two band integrals (corners[*].transfer) is the transfer #140 asks for -- measured, at every corner, with every integrate-phase noise source carrying its own transfer rather than one OTA-derived factor applied to all of them. Why this is the accumulating quantity: with the summing node at vcm+Vn in phi2 and the Cs top plates reset to vcm in phi1, charge conservation on the summing node gives a per-cycle state increment of (Csi+Csr)/Ci * Vn, independent of the summing-node parasitic Cp, while the static v(vod) noise gain is 1 + (Csi+Csr+Cp)/Ci. The ratio is therefore about 1/2 in amplitude on this sizing, where Ci is drawn equal to Csi+Csr. BOTH the baseband and the aliased part are re-referred this way, so neither keeps the old 1/C1-at-v(vod) treatment -- see corners[*].transfer.power_ratio_db_by_band, which reports them separately because the transfer is not the same in the two bands.

ktc.what: switch kT/C: the sampled voltage on the four input- and reference-branch sampling capacitors, differentially summed

amp.what: integrate phase: the OTA together with the phi2 switches that are in its loop -- spec 5.3's thermal share is 'sampling switches and amplifier', and the phi2 switches belong to the amplifier half of that split

ampq.what: integrate phase, accumulating part only: the same OTA and phi2 switches as `amp`, read as the differential voltage across Ci, which is the per-cycle output increment the next phi1 reset leaves on the integrator's state

method.lower_edge: every band integral starts at 1 Hz. Flicker noise diverges logarithmically downward, so this edge is a choice, not a property of the circuit: var_audio_band_V2 repeats the baseband integral from 20 Hz so the sensitivity is visible rather than hidden.

convergence.integration_scheme: klt_vs_ngspice_integral_rel compares klt's trapezoid against ngspice's own onoise_total over the same swept range, gated <= 0.01 per corner. What it shows: that the 20-points/decade grid resolves the spectrum well enough for a trapezoid to reproduce ngspice's own integrator. What it does NOT show: anything about the upper band edge -- both numbers span the identical sweep, so truncating the band would move them together and they would still agree. It is not cited as upper-edge evidence.
convergence.upper_edge: the per-corner evidence that F_HI = 1e+11 Hz is far enough out is in `upper_edge` below, and it is the direct test: the SAME integral over bands truncated at 1e+09 Hz and 1e+10 Hz. An integral with content left above its edge moves when the edge moves, so 1 - (rms_trunc/rms_tot)^2 is the measured share of the full-band variance lying above each truncated edge, and the ratio of the two is the per-decade shrink rate. extrapolated_frac_above_F_HI carries that same rate one decade further, past 1e+11 Hz. trunc_vs_total_rms_rel gates the 1e+10 Hz one at 0.1 per corner (a reference-validity limit, not a spec row). The density roll-off beside it (1e+10 Hz against 100 MHz) is the slope that produces this. summary.extrapolated_tail_margin_impact_db closes the loop on why this matters: it is what the whole residual tail would be worth on a budget margin, 10*log10(1 + frac), against the dB of margin the verdicts report.
convergence.closure: independently, for ktc: cs_eff_F = 4kT/var_total_V2 lands within switch- and plate-parasitic distance of the drawn Cs on every corner (see summary.cs_eff_F_range and method.chosen). A short integral would under-count the variance and so report a cs_eff ABOVE the drawn value by far more than parasitics can explain, so this is a second, physical check on the same band.

unit_conversions.per_event_to_inband: the sampled sequence is white across fs/2, so the share of a WHITE per-event variance that lands in BW is 1/OSR = 1/128. This is the link spec 5.3 assumes and the one model B's i.i.d. Gaussian draw reproduces: inband_white_V2 = var_total_V2 / OSR.
unit_conversions.non_white_correction: the measured spectra are not white, so inband_V2 splits them: the baseband share (below BW) reaches the band with no aliasing and is NOT divided by OSR, and only the share above BW folds. inband_V2 = var_baseband_V2 + var_aliased_V2 / OSR. For the switches the two links agree to a part in 1e4 (white); for the amplifier they do not, and the difference is its flicker content.
unit_conversions.volts_to_fs: 1 FS = VREFP - VREFN = 1.2 V of differential integrator output, and model B's integrator-1 coefficient is C1 = 0.5, so a variance referred to the integrator input in V^2 becomes (C1/1.2)^2 = 0.173611 times that in FS^2. Same convention as sim/integrator-ci's ci_offset.
unit_conversions.model_b_equivalent: model_b_equiv_ktc_noise_var_fs2 is the WHITE per-event variance that reproduces inband_V2 through model B's own 1/OSR link, i.e. inband_V2 * OSR converted to FS^2. That, not var_total_fs2, is the number to load into ktc_noise_var, because model B draws i.i.d. per clock and would otherwise under-count the flicker share.

budget.unchanged: both budgets are the ratified planning allocation and are reported against, not adjusted. A corner that misses is recorded as a miss and filed; resizing the OTA or the capacitors is out of scope here.
budget.flicker_caveat: 5.3 allocates a THERMAL share, and the per-corner amplifier numbers here are thermal PLUS flicker, so the comparison is conservative for the amplifier and exact for the switches. issue #140 now MEASURES that split, at one corner: see device_split.blocks.inband_nqci.flicker_share, which is the fraction of the accumulating in-band amplifier noise that is 1/f rather than thermal. The thermal-only part is thermal_and_shot_V2. 5.3 still carries no 1/f allocation at all, which remains a finding (#138 step 2 / #142), not a bench defect -- this bench reports against the ratified line unchanged and does not relax it.
budget.reported_twice: both budgets are reported against the pre-#140 static treatment (total_thermal_*) AND the #140 accumulating one (total_thermal_accumulated_*), with the SAME budget values, so the effect of the corrected referral on the verdict is visible rather than substituted silently.

leaves_out: flicker/thermal separation ACROSS THE GRID. issue #140 adds the split, but from one local corner (device_split, tt/1.800V/27C): klt sim still has no measurement form for ngspice's per-device, per-mechanism vectors, so the 45-corner requests cannot carry it. Filed under the friction protocol as 2AMLogic/klayout-tools#5553; the per-corner numbers in `corners` are therefore still thermal PLUS flicker.

correlation of the sampled noise between consecutive clocks, BEYOND the accumulating referral. issue #140 removes the part of the over-count that came from referring the non-accumulating summing-node excursion as if it accumulated (see method.accumulating_vs_static), and that correction is measured per corner. What is still left out is the correlation BETWEEN consecutive accumulated increments: ampq's increments are still treated as i.i.d. per event, so the in-band effect of the amplifier's 1/f is still over-counted, and any correlated-double-sampling benefit is still ignored. This bench's phi1 reset is to vcm, not a CDS reset, so there is no CDS benefit to claim here.

the summing-node parasitic Cp is not measured. transfer.implied_summing_node_cp_F inverts the measured in-band amplitude ratio for it, which is a derived indicative value, not an extraction: the ratio it inverts is the composite over every phi2 noise source, and it is quotable in band only because the device split shows the OTA's own devices carry essentially all of the in-band noise there. It is not quotable for the aliased part, where the phi2 switches do matter.

the last Cp term of the accumulating read, which makes these numbers CONSERVATIVE rather than optimistic. For OTA input-referred noise the true per-cycle increment is (Csi+Csr)/Ci * Vn, while a STATIC read across Ci gives (Csi+Csr+Cp)/Ci * Vn: Cp's charge on Ci does not change across a cycle, so it leaves the increment but not this measurement. The size of that residual is reported as device_split.ota_input_referred_transfer.inband.static_across_ci_over_counts_by_db, derived from the implied Cp. Removing it would IMPROVE the reported margin, so it is left in rather than corrected out on a derived number.

the large-signal phi1 hold error of issue #147. The transfer measured here is small-signal about the operating point with no large differential input, so a large-signal Sci hold error does not enter it. #147's Sci condition (Vgs = Vdda - vcm) is worst at low Vdda and cold, so if a per-corner transfer looks like an outlier at the 1.620 V/-40 C corners, #147 is the known candidate rather than a new finding.
the finite duration of the integrate phase: the amplifier integral is taken over the circuit's own noise bandwidth, not truncated to the 97.66 ns phase
reference and bias noise (DR-005: inputs at the boundary, ideal and noiseless here)
clock-jitter-induced noise (model B's jitter_rms_s, not extracted from this block)
mismatch (this is the nominal grid, no Monte Carlo) and layout parasitics (DR-001 item 4, post-layout)

conditions.corner_set: DR-002 full grid, 5 process x 3 T x 3 Vdda

drawn_capacitors.method: drawn W/L of the cell's sky130_fd_pr__cap_mim_m3_1 devices through the PDK's own area/perimeter model (camimc 2e-15 F/um^2, cpmimc 1.9e-16 F/um, m3_dw -0.025 um) at the TYPICAL cap section. The cap_low/cap_high sections move camimc by -11%/+12%, so this single number is a reference, not a per-corner value -- the per-corner cs_eff_F below is derived from each corner's own simulated variance and does carry that spread, plus the switch and plate parasitics the drawn capacitance alone does not.

inband.over_count_note: the static across-Ci read includes Cp's share of the charge on Ci, which does NOT change across a cycle (the OTA holds the summing node at its own input offset in both phases), so it drops out of the true per-cycle increment but not out of this measurement. Derived from the implied Cp, so indicative, and it makes the recorded accumulating numbers conservative, not optimistic.

audio.over_count_note: the static across-Ci read includes Cp's share of the charge on Ci, which does NOT change across a cycle (the OTA holds the summing node at its own input offset in both phases), so it drops out of the true per-cycle increment but not out of this measurement. Derived from the implied Cp, so indicative, and it makes the recorded accumulating numbers conservative, not optimistic.

device_split.ota_input_referred_transfer_note: AC 1 of issue #140: the transfer from OTA input-referred noise to the accumulated per-cycle increment, isolated from the composite by summing only the OTA's own devices at each output. The composite the record actually applies per corner is corners[*].transfer; this block is what says how much of that composite is the OTA transfer and how much is the switches', and it is the one that the issue's hand analysis predicts.
device_split.result_kind: simulated (one local ngspice corner, transistor-level; a raw `ngspice -b` because klt sim has no measurement form for the per-device vectors). A simulated number is never called measured.
device_split.method: ngspice emits a per-device, per-mechanism breakdown of the integrated noise only when the noise statement carries a pts_per_summary argument (1000000, above the point count, so one summary). The vectors hold each contribution as an RMS in VOLTS, so they are squared before summing; closure_* below is the proof of that reading -- the summed per-device and per-mechanism variances must reproduce onoise_total^2 to 1e-06, and the run refuses to record a split that does not. Summing the vectors as if they were variances over-counts by about 4e4 on this block.
device_split.deck: the committed integrator_noise_ampq.cir verbatim, wrapped at run time in the .lib/.control/.end a raw ngspice run needs; same circuit, same probes and same deck_sha256 as the grid run
device_split.one_corner_only: the DR-002 anchor tt/1.800 V/27 C, which is what AC 3 of issue #140 asks for at minimum. The 45-corner grid carries the TRANSFER at every corner; only this decomposition is single-corner, and it is a mechanism attribution, not a budget number.
device_split.mechanism_note: `1overf` is flicker; every other mechanism (id, rd, rs, rg, rb*) is thermal, and ig* is gate-leakage shot noise, zero on this block. So thermal_and_shot_V2 is the thermal share spec 5.3 actually allocates.
